- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class), deletePackage (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f9b421716dd79df6c7c3a34bbd5a3a9f425e84f4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ff4d3ca2d456f5fa3bf23969763fd935e093b911` — the merge of head `7d36e8d205d783c9171b952d66dc06b16fa15ae0` into base `f9b421716dd79df6c7c3a34bbd5a3a9f425e84f4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ff4d3ca2d456f5fa3bf23969763fd935e093b911 && git checkout ff4d3ca2d456f5fa3bf23969763fd935e093b911
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f9b421716dd79df6c7c3a34bbd5a3a9f425e84f4 7d36e8d205d783c9171b952d66dc06b16fa15ae0 && git checkout -B drift-repro f9b421716dd79df6c7c3a34bbd5a3a9f425e84f4 && git merge --no-ff 7d36e8d205d783c9171b952d66dc06b16fa15ae0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f9b421716dd79df6c7c3a34bbd5a3a9f425e84f4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f9b421716dd79df6c7c3a34bbd5a3a9f425e84f4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

`Check Changeset` is red by design on this head: a deliberate correction of a pending release note · `domain:spec` seat 4 · `session_0121ooBYRmS8ziFXm9ai5YHm` · 2026-10-14T15:19Z

**The gate and why it is red.** On `7d36e8d205`, `check-empty-changeset.mjs` refuses because this PR changes `.changeset/23415-drop-storage-other-rows.md`, a changeset it did not add. It is the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class, not a collision.
- Per ruling D on #18375 (`5729188290`, maintainer 「同意」 2026-09-18), the confirmation is written on the PR, in the maintainer's own word or carried by a seat with provenance. The gate stays advisory red.
- `Check Changeset` is not a required context, and its workflow (`pr-automation.yml`) runs on `pull_request` only, never on `merge_group`.
- ⛔ `skip-changeset` is not applied.

**The note, and what changed under it.**
- The note is `.changeset/23415-drop-storage-other-rows.md` (#23415 → PR #23464, merged `1baf976cf9`, not yet released), this seat's own landing.
- Its TO said an uninstall "reports the refusal for that object in its `failed[]` list … and leaves the object's row and table in place".
- This PR makes the whole uninstall refuse `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` before anything is removed, so that sentence would ship false. It now reads: "An uninstall of a package holding such an object, without `keepData`, is refused whole, `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, before anything is removed; its message names the object, the rows that keep it, and the ways out."
- Nothing else in that note changed. Its FROM ("The same held for … an uninstall") is the released behaviour and stays.
- In the same stroke, this PR's own note (`.changeset/23473-uninstall-shared-object-refusal.md`) moved its FROM from `main`'s unreleased intermediate (`400 PACKAGE_DELETE_PARTIAL`) to the last release's behaviour: the shared table was dropped while the other row still served the object.

**Confirmation:** requested from the maintainer in the seat's session. This PR does not enter the queue before the maintainer's word is recorded here. Also still owed: the at-tier contract review and the seat record.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7d36e8d205d783c9171b952d66dc06b16fa15ae0`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23473 (body; lane decision `6168058499`; claim `6168221878`; dev report `6170924033`; addendum `6172200644`); PR #23504 (body, file list, the diff against `main` re-fetched at this head, byte-equal to the three-dot net diff ignoring index lines: 4 files, +402/-1); `.changeset/23415-drop-storage-other-rows.md` on `origin/main` (at 1418de4c7e) versus this head; `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml` and `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs` (identical on `origin/main` and the head); the ruleset for `main`; the published dist-tags of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`; and the head's 40 check-runs, read last. Not read: the `Collected` comment on the card, the PR comment that opens with the Check Changeset sentence, any seat self-check comment. The PR is a draft from the base repository, 402/1 lines, no governed path, model-free commit trailers.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The narrowing itself: right.** `deletePackage` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, between step 3 and step 4) now throws `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` / 409 when `keepData` is not `true` and an active, non-`sys_` object row of the package has, at its address, another package's active row or the package-less active row. The door (`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`, the `catch` around `protocol.deletePackage`) answers the thrown status and code as it already did for step 3, before it touches the registry or the disable record; so `DELETE /api/v1/packages/:id` answers `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with nothing removed, where `main` answers `400 PACKAGE_DELETE_PARTIAL` over a package whose `sys_packages` row is already gone. Shape B of the lane decision; #21276's guarantee ("nothing durable before step 4") holds, the pre-flight only reads, and the docblock's numbering is unchanged.
2. **The pre-flight asks exactly the per-item delete's question: right, on every element.** (a) Rows: the step-2 read (`sys_metadata` where `package_id` is the package, all states); drafts and rows without a string `name` are skipped, the same split the per-item loop makes for `state`. (b) Type fold: `canonicalMetaType` then `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR`; `deleteMetaItem` folds through `canonicalizeMetaRequestType` (the same `canonicalMetaType`, plus a refusal for an unrecognised spelling of a declared type) and then `singularTypeForRepo`, the same `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` fold. A spelling that refusal would catch never folds to `object`, so it drops no table on either side. (c) Guard: `shouldDropStorage(type, name, true, 'active')` is the per-item call with the `dropStorage: true` and `state: 'active'` the loop sends for an active row when `keepData !== true` (object only, active only, never `sys_`). (d) Address: `packagelessAddress(type, name, undefined, 'active')`; `deleteMetaItem` passes `member = resolveBundleMemberSelector(type, undefined)`, which returns `undefined`, and `overlayMemberWhere('object', undefined)` is `{}`, so both read `where: { type, name, state: 'active', organization_id: null }`. (e) Verdict: the pre-flight refuses when the package is among `candidates` and another candidate or `unbound` remains; `deleteMetaItem` refuses when the package's row exists, `dropsStorage` holds, and `remainingPackages` is non-empty or `unbound` with a non-null `packageId`, and `packageId` is always the package here. The same predicate; when the package holds no org-null active row at the address the per-item delete answers "nothing was deleted" without refusing, and the pre-flight continues. (f) The per-item object delete reaches that refusal site: `object` carries `allowRuntimeCreate: true` (`packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts:786`), so `useRepoPath` is true and the legacy raw-engine drop, which has no remaining-rows check, is not on the object path. (g) The `asked` set is keyed by name only, but is written only after the object guard, so it collapses nothing but a legacy organization-scoped duplicate, which the loop removes through `removeLegacyOrganizationRowOnUninstall` with no table drop and which `packagelessAddress` never counts.
3. **`keepData: true` skips it: right.** The whole block sits under `request.keepData !== true`, the predicate that also decides `dropStorage` for the loop; with `keepData` nothing is read, and since no per-item `dropStorage` is sent, nothing drops or refuses later either. The door sends `keepData: true` for `?keepData=true` or `?keepData=1`, so the changeset's prescription is the door's spelling.
4. **A failed read is the step-2 read failure: right.** `packagelessAddress` tolerates only an unprovisioned store and rethrows every other failure; the pre-flight wraps any throw in `metadataReadFailureError`, step 2's own classifier (the non-quoting 503, or a marked application refusal). An unprovisioned store cannot reach the pre-flight: step 2 deliberately does not tolerate it and throws first.
5. **Nothing durable before it: right.** Steps 1 to 3 are pure or reads; the pre-flight reads; step 4's `packageStore.delete` is still the first write. Pinned: the `sys_packages` row, `GET` 200, both rows, the table, the record and the registry entry are intact after the refusal.
6. **Reused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, no code minted: right.** It is the code `dropStorageRemainingRowsRefusal` answers for the same rows on the per-item path (environment state, not the request: the same uninstall is accepted once the other rows or the package's own row are gone), so the metadata door and the package door speak one code for one condition. Step 3's extender refusal is a code-less `Error` from `SchemaRegistry.assertPackageUninstallable` (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:4256`), which the door answers `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` (pinned at `package-uninstall-store-refusal.integration.test.ts:265`); copying that family would hand an operator a server-fault status with a withheld message for a condition the caller can act on. Right not to copy it; step 3's own code is #23505, not this PR.
7. **The refusal text: right.** Prescription first ("Uninstall package 'P' with keepData (?keepData=true; keepData: true in process), which keeps all its object tables, or first delete, without dropStorage, its row or the other rows of each object below (DELETE /api/v1/meta/object/NAME?package=ID)"), then the fact ("Nothing was removed: an uninstall drops an object's table only with the object's last row, and N objects of this package are also held by other rows:"), then the list, each object with `remainingRowsPhrase` naming its other holders (up to five packages, and the package-less row), the list cut at five objects with "; and N more". Two ways out, the second answering the card body's concern with shape B (the package's own row deleted first keeps the shared table and still lets the uninstall drop the private tables; pinned as case 4). Singular and plural forms both spelled. No tracker number in the runtime string. The `?keepData=true` spelling matches the door.
8. **The two callers: neither worse off.** The door: the same `catch`, the same "nothing was touched on this path" (registry and disable record untouched until the verb answers), now 409 with an intact package instead of 400 over a half-removed one. `rollBackUnmanagedImport`: it uninstalls the new base without `keepData`; the import refused any name an `organization_id: null` stored row of any binding already holds (`unmanagedImportCollisions`) before writing, so the pre-flight can fire there only on a row written between that read and the rollback. In that race `main` left the base half-uninstalled (`sys_packages` gone, `failedCount` above 0); the head catches the throw, reports "the uninstall failed: ..." in the import's error and the operator log, and leaves the base whole and uninstallable. Not worse.
9. **The real-stack pin: right, and it pins what the changeset says.** `packages/runtime/src/package-uninstall-shared-object.integration.test.ts`: real `ObjectQL` over better-sqlite3 on disk, the real `PackageServicePlugin`, the real protocol, the real `HttpDispatcher.handlePackages`; the store is read through knex, not the door's word. Case 1 asserts status and code, the message's object, holder and `keepData`, and the full untouched state including the running registry; case 2 seeds the package-less row at rest (the only honest way, since the save door resolves a package-less save to the package's row); case 3 pins the `keepData` way out, `failed: []`, registry served by Q; case 4 pins the own-row-first way out with the private table dropped and the shared one kept; case 5 is the single-package control. Not pinned, and not required by the card: the cut at five objects and the plural wording (the PR body's measured two-object sample shows the plural), and a draft row of the shared object by another package on the uninstall path (the per-item note already fixes drafts as not counting; the pre-flight reads `'active'` only).
10. **Public surface: unchanged, right.** No export, type, schema or error code is added, removed or renamed; `DeletePackageRequest` is as it was. `Clause-②: no` is truthful.
11. Observed, not a defect of this PR: the loop's other per-item refusals (lock, packaged base, origin gate) still arrive after step 4 and ride `failed[]`, as on `main`; PR #23469 owns that loop. Cost: one `sys_metadata` read per active object row of the package without `keepData`, none with it.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/23473-uninstall-shared-object-refusal.md`: `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': minor`, a `fix(metadata-protocol)!:` summary, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, the BREAKING banner "shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention", and one adr-0087 marker comment reading `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Consistent: the `(narrowing)` arm is the breaking declaration the gates read (AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3; `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`), `major` is refused in the window and breaking-ness rides the banner plus the disposition (`pr-automation.yml`). The disposition is honest: nothing authorable, exported or stored is removed, renamed or rewritten; the remedy lives in the request (`keepData`, or delete a row first), and the Remedy section is prose, not a code rewrite, so the category's prescription check holds, confirmed by CI: step 13 of the Check Changeset job ("Require an ADR-0087 disposition on a declared-breaking changeset") is success on this head. Only `metadata-protocol` is bumped; `runtime` gains a test file and no published code, so no bump is owed there.
- `Clause-②: no` on the claim and the PR body: right, the diff widens no accept set and adds no public key; the arm sits in the changeset, where the gate reads it.
- FROM: the published dist-tags are `latest` 17.7.0 and `next` 18.0.0-next.1; `.changeset/23415-drop-storage-other-rows.md` is still pending on `origin/main` (one of 27 pending notes) and no CHANGELOG section carries its text, so PR #23464's per-item 409 and the `failed[]` / `400 PACKAGE_DELETE_PARTIAL` shape have never shipped. The last release's uninstall of P, for an object P and Q both hold, removed P's row and dropped the table (#23415's FROM: "The same held ... for an uninstall"), leaving Q's definition served over no table, next data read `500`. The 23473 FROM says exactly that and names no `PACKAGE_DELETE_PARTIAL`. Right for a reader upgrading from 17.7.0 or 18.0.0-next.1. The summary line's "instead of dropping the object's table while the other row still serves it" matches.
- The 23415 edit, judged sentence by sentence: the diff to that file is one line (+1/-1); frontmatter, summary, `Clause-②`, the adr-0087 marker, the banner, FROM (including "and for an uninstall (`deletePackage`, ...)"), Unchanged and Remedy are byte-identical to `origin/main`. Removed: "An uninstall reports the refusal for that object in its `failed[]` list, as it reports any per-item refusal, and leaves the object's row and table in place." True only between PR #23464 and this PR, false once this lands. Written: "An uninstall of a package holding such an object, without `keepData`, is refused whole, `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, before anything is removed; its message names the object, the rows that keep it, and the ways out." True after this PR (① 1, 5, 7). Both notes are pending for the same release, so the two TO sentences agree when they ship. The sentence stands without a cross-reference; see ③.
- `Check Changeset` red: job 115934636963 on this head, step 12 ("Reject an empty-frontmatter changeset added by this PR", the `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs` run) is the only failure; steps 11 (Require a changeset), 13 (ADR-0087 disposition) and 15 (major guard) are success. The script's foreign-changeset rule refuses every `M` row of a `.changeset/*.md` present at the merge base, and this PR's `.changeset` rows are one `A` (23473) and one `M` (23415): the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class, whose remedy in the script and in the workflow's route 0 is do not restore it, do not apply `skip-changeset`, confirm on the PR, leave the check red. That is the only reason it is red. It is not a required context: the `main` ruleset (12119582) requires `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, all success on this head; `pr-automation.yml` runs on `pull_request` only, never `merge_group`. The three conditions for carrying a designed red into the queue hold: the source says so, the job does not run in the queue, and the PR carries a comment naming the gate and the reason; for a PR that also changes code, this same-head record is the confirmation, and it names the note and the sentence above.
- Check-runs on this head: 40; 33 success, 6 skipped (the full-battery set: Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood shard matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance), 1 failure (`Check Changeset`, above), 0 in progress.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report `6170924033`, deviations:
1. Two print-only scratch tests placed and deleted, never committed. Answered: the head's file list is four files, no residue.
2. One suite run outlived the 600 s foreground cap and was waited on by its recorded PID. Answered: a harness mechanic; the verdict is CI's, and `Test Core` 1/6 to 6/6 and the aggregate are success on this head.
3. One locked call joined two sweeps with `;`. Answered the same way; the post-merge rerun used `&&`, and CI is the reading of record.
4. `ablation-dist-preflight` once refused on an untracked scratch file during a plain rebuild. Answered: read as no measurement, no gate result was claimed from it; the ablation itself is one-shot evidence, not a gate.

Dev report, out-of-scope findings:
1. The 23415 sentence. Edited in the addendum round and judged true in ②; the red it causes is the designed class. Closed here.
2. After a `keepData` uninstall or an own-row delete, the running registry serves Q's definition and data reads answer. The expected outcome of Q's row keeping the object defined; measured, pinned (cases 3 and 4), no action.

Addendum `6172200644`, deviations:
1. The tracker number left out of the 23415 sentence (the suggested text said "see the 23473 changeset"). Accepted: the sentence states the new behaviour in full and needs no pointer; the 23473 note ships in the same release.
2. The 23473 summary line changed to name the released behaviour. Accepted: it follows the FROM correction and matches it.
3. "Docs: no edit". Checked on the head: `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx:501` ("every row bound to it ... `?keepData=true` keeps the object tables"), `content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx:135` ("Uninstall a package.") and the generated `package-api.mdx` `keepData` row say nothing about what an uninstall does to a shared object's table and list no status for it; nothing is falsified. The docs-drift bot's rows come from the `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` literal and the class symbol, not from a restated rule. Accepted.
4. The merge of `origin/main` without a source re-test. Accepted under AGENTS.md Multi-agent discipline item 10 (none of the 10 commits touches `protocol.ts` or the packages domain), and CI ran the full PR set on the merged tree.

Nothing escalated. `open_questions` is empty on both reports.

## 席位核对

`domain:spec` seat 4 (#18917) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_0121ooBYRmS8ziFXm9ai5YHm` · claim `6168221878` on #23473 · reviewed head `7d36e8d205d783c9171b952d66dc06b16fa15ae0` · 2026-10-14T16:03Z

**Verdict: ACCEPT, landing held on the maintainer's confirmation (clause d).** Not governed. 4 files, +402 / −1. The `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review on this head passed (`6172644842`).

1. **Shape.**
   - Draft. First line `Fixes #23473`. `Clause-②: no` at line start.
   - The changeset `.changeset/23473-uninstall-shared-object-refusal.md`: `metadata-protocol` `minor`, BREAKING, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.
   - The one-sentence correction of the pending note `.changeset/23415-drop-storage-other-rows.md` is the DELIBERATE CORRECTION described on the PR (`6171760091`).
2. **Premises against the dispatch (lane decision B, `6168058499`).**
   - The pre-flight asks exactly the per-item delete's question: the same rows, type fold, `shouldDropStorage` guard, `packagelessAddress` read and verdict predicate. The review checked each element.
   - It is skipped under `keepData: true`.
   - A failed read is the step-2 read failure.
   - Nothing durable happens before step 4.
   - No measured flow needs shape C.
3. **Gates and evidence.**
   - Head check-runs: 33 success, 6 skipped (the full-battery set), 1 failure, 0 in progress.
   - The failure is `Check Changeset`, step 12 (`check-empty-changeset.mjs`) alone, on the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class. That red is by design:
     - the source says to leave it red (`pr-automation.yml` route 0);
     - the job runs on `pull_request` only, never on `merge_group`;
     - the PR names the gate and the cause (`6171760091`).
   - All five required contexts are success.
   - The dev's local reconciliation: 65 of 65 at `fee128e3da`, and 64 of 65 at this head (the one exception is the designed red).
   - The real-stack pin passed 5/5. The ablation went red on cases 1–2 and was restored.
4. **Accepted deviations.**
   - The file surface was extended by the seat for the patch round, to the 23415 note.
   - The 23415 sentence states the new behaviour without a tracker number, because shipped text carries none.
   - The 23473 summary line now names the released behaviour.
   - No docs edit: the review re-checked the pages the docs-drift check named.
5. **Out-of-scope dispositions.**
   - Step 3's extension refusal answers `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`: filed as #23505.
   - The loop's other per-item refusals still arrive after step 4. That loop belongs to PR #23469, another lane: noted, no carrier here.
6. **Landing clauses.**
   - (a) The `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS on the landing head: met (`6172644842`).
   - (b) Every required check green, every other check green or skipped by design, and `Check Changeset` red by design only: met at this reading.
   - (c) `mergeable_state` clean at enqueue. GitHub reports `unstable` for the one designed red; the required set is green.
   - (d) Per ruling D on #18375 (`5729188290`), the correction of a pending release note is confirmed on the PR in the maintainer's own words, or by a seat carrying them with provenance. **Pending:** it has been requested from the maintainer in the seat's session.
